items.title: Hands on with the Honkai: Star Rail v4.0 experience
items.summary: This HoyoVerse train just keeps on chugging!
items.content:
The last article I wrote for Honkai: Star Rail was going over the details of the upcoming Version 4.0 release . Since then, HoYoverse generously offered up the opportunity to play Version 4.0 and experience Planarcadia early. Having spent about a dozen hours or so playing with the new characters, experiencing the story, and generally taking in the sights and sounds of Planarcadia, I’m prepared to share my thoughts on all of it.

It’s best to start off with the main attraction of Version 4.0: Planarcadia. This new planet is a fictional world come to life and boy does it leave a fantastic first impression. Full of the kind of sights and sounds you’d expect from an Asian city brimming with life. Exploration is a blast with all the alleys and little nooks to find, the platforming segments that can either help you navigate across certain parts of the city or find chests within them. There’s also a new style of puzzles that require you to rotate a 2D plane in a 3D space to “paint” certain parts of it to make them solid and let you platform with those objects. Planarcadia is so full of whimsy and still has some of the overhang of a crime family really enabling a super unique feeling planet compared to what we’ve had with previous locations such as the Xianzhou or Amphoreus.

The two new characters following the path of Elation feel great, even if the Aha Moment is a little overstimulating sometimes. Sparxie and Yao Guang fit on a team together like a glove to demolish all the bosses I’ve thrown them against. I’m eager to see where the new path goes with time, especially since we only have the two characters currently. Even as of the live public server branch, we’re unsure when Elation Trailblazer will make their debut, so keep an eye on that as versions progress beyond 4.0. You’ll need to get a hold of new Elation Light Cones as well since they obviously can’t use the other Paths’ options. Burning skill points to increase the Elation stacks until Aha decides he’s satisfied and steps in for a big attack feels really great and it has me curious what future Elation characters might do when they trigger their own Aha Moments.

Not to mention that for new players, you’ve got the opportunity to really kickstart a team of your choice with a new planet. We’re at a point in the game where there’s so many options for characters you can pick from and build around, and 4.0 introducing Elation means that as a new player, you can jump in and get a headstart on pulling for that archetype. Especially with a new Novaflare round of buffs, there’s even more options than before bringing older characters back into the limelight. The Black Swan and Sparkle buffs are so massive that people running DoT teams or any team using an action advance support such as Bronya or Sunday have another insane option. Sparkle was always good, but her Novaflare enables her to further buff your DPS units to extreme levels. Black Swan’s Novaflare was even more insane and rocketed her back up to the top for damage even as a DoT unit. Combined with the option to pick a free character including units like Sparkle, Kafka (who works great in DoT teams), and more, you really can’t go wrong in Planarcadia and the Version 4.0 patch from what I’ve gotten to experience.

Between the free characters, the great change of pace in the story from the latter half of Amphoreus (if you’ve played it, you know), the new cityscape that is quite honestly my new favorite location in the game, and all the new characters to look forward to, you really should make a return to Star Rail if you’ve been away for a minute and are curious about where we’re at. If you’re new, definitely consider giving it a shot. There’s even a bonus to let you convert trace materials for leveling character skills at a 1 to 1 ratio this time instead of a 2 for 1, so you really can kickstart your Elation team. With characters being important again like Silver Wolf, Blade, and Himeko, as well as new faces like Sparxie, Yao Guang, Ashveil, and Pearl, I think 4.0 is just the start of a real treat of a patch cycle for Honkai: Star Rail.

items.title: Honkai: Nexus Anima Preview: HoYoverse’s Next Big Hit?
items.summary: Our Honkai: Nexus Anima preview explores HoYoverse’s colourful creature collector, covering auto-battles, team-building, and gacha mechanics.
items.content:
The gacha game landscape gets substantially busier every time HoYoverse announces a new title. Genshin Impact propelled the company into the stratosphere, while Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero have since catered to different tastes and helped the developer reach even more corners of the gaming world.

With that in mind, it isn’t surprising to see HoYoverse turn its attention to creature collecting with Honkai: Nexus Anima .

Honkai: Nexus Anima is a little bit of a lot of things. It combines HoYoverse’s familiar taste for dark, twisted storytelling with what might be the company’s most colourful world yet. Almost every corner bursts with detail, helped by the fact that this universe isn’t populated by people alone. It is also home to plenty of adorable monsters.

These creatures, known as Anima, have designs that wouldn’t look out of place in Pokémon. Instead of being divided into conventional elemental categories, however, they have more abstract, mood-driven attributes based on concepts such as Satiation and Dreams. It gives the game’s creatures a distinct identity, even if its inspirations are easy to spot.

You’ll use your Anima in auto-battles, with success largely depending on choosing creatures that work well together and placing them in effective positions. The characters you have access to provide special abilities, while fielding particular combinations of Anima can grant additional bonuses.

The battles themselves aren’t especially complicated, but there appears to be plenty of depth in building an effective team. You’ll want to spend time exploring and catching creatures, both to expand your tactical options and to make your existing Anima stronger.

That progression loop could prove compelling. There is something undeniably satisfying about watching the numbers rise, particularly when each improvement gives you another reason to experiment with your line-up.

The gacha system is split between pulling for characters, who provide new abilities, and pulling for Anima to obtain higher-rarity versions or upgrade those already in your collection. Anima can also be caught in the wild, which makes the monetisation side of the game a little unusual.

The full release will presumably encourage players to pull for the strongest creatures, but being able to find lower-rarity Anima and improve them through play is promising. It may give players the freedom to make their favourites viable by investing time rather than money.

Of course, this is still a gacha game, so monetisation will inevitably be part of the experience. Even if Honkai: Nexus Anima proves relatively welcoming to free-to-play players, it will still be designed to encourage spending.

I enjoy auto-battlers, but their hands-off nature can sometimes make them less engaging over time. Honkai: Nexus Anima’s progression systems should help keep players invested, although much will depend on the variety of challenges available beyond the main campaign.

HoYoverse has become increasingly good at creating entertaining side modes in its recent games, so there is every reason to expect more than a straightforward journey through the story. Whether those additional activities can keep the team-building interesting in the long term remains to be seen.

While I like most of what I’ve seen so far, the story feels a little flimsy. Once again, we play as a protagonist with no memory, a device that is starting to feel like a crutch in games of this kind. It makes delivering exposition easier, but there is something frustrating about beginning another adventure as a character who knows almost nothing about themselves or the world around them.

The villains are more encouraging. They bring a slightly more sinister edge to the otherwise colourful setting, and although the narrative currently feels a little crowded, there is real potential for this to become one of HoYoverse’s darkest stories yet. Given the territory explored by games such as Genshin Impact, that is no small claim.

items.title: "Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.5 "To Roll the Stars in Astropolis" is Coming Soon"
items.summary: 'To Roll the Stars in Astropolis' content will make sense to players who love a bit of Waveflair in the summer.
items.content:
SINGAPORE, August 14, 2026 — Global interactive entertainment brand HoYoverse announced today that the new Version 4.5 of its title Honkai: Star Rail, "To Roll the Stars in Astropolis," will officially launch on August 26, 2026. Facing a crisis triggered by the Voracity, the Trailblazer will officially depart for Astropolis, a key Interastral Peace Corporation stronghold, to seek aid for the disaster-stricken Planarcadia. In addition, the Trailblazer will have the opportunity to embark on a special summer vacation with Robin and Aventurine. Click to watch the Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.5 trailer: https://youtu.be/hTIdycp-c9Y Click here to access the media kit: https://hoyoverse.box.com/s/61n3qpa5t60i6smrkc3gxxp1xc3uka3d Following the Express Crew's victory over Lord Ravager Asat Pramad, the Voracity makes THEIR official appearance, once again plunging Planarcadia into a fatal crisis. To find the crucial strength needed to aid Planarcadia, the Trailblazer will attempt to evade the Voracity's obstruction and officially depart for Astropolis, the headquarters of the Interastral Peace Entertainment. There, the Trailblazer will navigate the complex hierarchy of the IPC's upper management to secure the key power required to help Planarcadia survive this calamity. As the crown jewel of the IPC's business empire, Astropolis not only embodies the elegant lifestyle of Interastral Peace Corporation workers and executives, but also serves as the vacation destination of choice for countless envoys, tycoons, and officials from across the Pan-Cosmic Trade System. In the story of this Trailblaze Continuance, which takes place either shortly or a long time after the journey in Planarcadia concludes, the Trailblazer will embark on an unforgettable interstellar vacation in Astropolis alongside Robin and Aventurine. In this update, the 5-star Wind character on the Path of Remembrance, Robin • Summeretto, will officially debut. Since Sunday left Penacony, Robin has taken over as the head of the Oak Family. This time, Robin isn't just here to perform, but is also on a secret mission to investigate Gopher Wood's "legacy." However, this superstar's stage isn't limited to concert venues. In combat, Robin • Summeretto will also take the stage and sing alongside her little bird band, providing buffs for the team. At the same time, her teammates' actions will accumulate Vibes for Robin • Summeretto. After she uses her Skill and her Vibes reach a certain level, her voice will bring the team to a Fever Pitch. Whenever allies attack the enemy, they will gain buffs, and the more frequently allies take action, the stronger the buffs Robin • Summeretto provides. Furthermore, when Robin • Summeretto uses her Ultimate, she can make a designated teammate immediately take action and regenerate Energy, while simultaneously increasing her own Vibes. It's also worth noting that in this story, Robin • Summeretto will debut her brand-new single, Only by Chasing the Wind, delivering a summery burst of vitality and surprises to fans in Astropolis and across the cosmos! In the second half of the version, the 5-star Quantum character on the Path of Elation, Aventurine • Waveflair, will make his debut. Despite kicking off a leisurely vacation in Astropolis, Aventurine continues to secretly leverage his connections and bargaining chips, vowing to verify his conjectures about the traitor among the Ten Stonehearts one by one. As a sports enthusiast and avid surfer, Aventurine • Waveflair attacks enemies in combat using a beach volleyball or by surfing the waves. Whenever he uses an ability or a teammate takes action, Aventurine • Waveflair can accumulate Punchline and Fervor. When Fervor reaches a certain number of points, he immediately triggers an extra Elation Skill. This not only attacks all enemies but also deals multiple instances of random single-target DMG. During the next Aha Instant, Aventurine • Waveflair's Elation Skill is further enhanced. The more actions the team takes, the higher the DMG dealt by the Elation Skill. After the version update, the drop rate for the limited 5-star character Robin • Summeretto and the limited 5-star Light Cone "Rise and Sing" will be boosted. The limited 5-star character Hyacine will concurrently receive a rerun, and the 4-star Light Cone "A Little Getaway" will also be added to the first half's Event Warps. Starting September 12, the drop rate for the limited 5-star character Aventurine • Waveflair and the limited 5-star Light Cone "Summer Rides the Surf" will be boosted, and the limited 5-star character Ashveil will also receive a rerun. In terms of version events, the racing event "Overdrive: Whirlwind Grand Prix" will officially kick off! The Trailblazer will step up as a team principal, leading their crew to become the brightest new stars on the track. Additionally, the "Minuscule Great Adventure" event will be launching simultaneously, allowing the Trailblazer to experience some fun and relaxing stage challenges. At the same time, the Divergent Universe is getting a gameplay update. The "Planar Fissure" and "Realm of the Strange" double-drop events, alongside a brand-new piece of Trailblaze Fashion, the electronic emoti standee headwear "Aw, Look Up Here," will all be going live as well. As for the story mission experience, starting from Version 4.5, story dialogue can be sped up. Players can toggle this feature on or off at any time during story dialogue. Finally, Honkai: Star Rail has officially announced its collaboration with MOONDROP. Sparxie-themed collaboration products and various online and offline events will gradually roll out across multiple regions worldwide, with more details to be revealed soon. Later this year, Honkai: Star Rail will also launch a surprise collaboration with Zenless Zone Zero. Characters from the world of Zenless Zone Zero will join the Trailblaze on a cosmic adventure, so stay tuned for more details! Honkai: Star Rail is now available on PC, iOS, Android, Epic Games Store, and PS5™, and has officially exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms. In 2023, the game won Apple's App Store iPhone Game of the Year, Google Play's Best Game, and BEST MOBILE GAME by The Game Awards. In 2024, it received the Golden Joystick Awards Still Playing Award (Mobile) and PlayStation Partner Awards 2024 PARTNER AWARD among other honors. The game has been rated Teen by the ESRB and is also classified as PEGI 12. For more details and updates, please visit https://hsr.hoyoverse.com/ or follow @HonkaiStarRail on Twitter (X), Instagram, and Facebook. About Honkai: Star Rail Honkai: Star Rail is a space fantasy RPG title with a journey through immense worlds of the unknown. The player takes on the role of "Trailblazer," a courageous individual implanted with a powerful artifact, Stellaron, and bearing the determination to unravel the mysteries surrounding the fabled "Cancer of All Worlds" and Aeons. The game features fantasy elements with myths and legends integrated into the space sci-fi story. Combined with the intuitive turn-based combat system, diverse and distinctive companions, and immersive storylines that together compose an interstellar melody filled with captivating worlds, each brimming with unique cultures, awe-inspiring landscapes, and mythical wonders to explore. About HoYoverse HoYoverse is committed to providing immersive virtual world experiences to players around the world. We have brought fans popular games including Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, Honkai Impact 3rd, Tears of Themis, and Zenless Zone Zero, as well as a wide range of entertainment content. Community is at the heart of everything we do. We are devoted to engaging fans and fostering an enthusiastic and inclusive global community that provides access and encouragement for people to share their passion for ACG (Animation, Comics, and Games) through their own creativity and skills. Pushing the boundaries of imagination, we consistently explore cutting-edge game development technologies, and have accumulated leading technical capabilities in cel shading, cloud gaming, and other fields. In the future, we will continue to expand our content production, technology research, and publishing duties through operations in offices in Singapore, Montreal, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Seoul, and other areas. items.title: Ugreen’s Honkai Star Rail power bank set brings gaming flair to Bangkok’s daily commute
items.summary: A new collaboration between technology accessories brand Ugreen and the hit mobile game Honkai Star Rail is turning an everyday necessity into something far more eye catching. Leading the limited edition collection is a magnetic power bank inspired by the popular character Yao Guang, combining distinctive design with practical charging performance that could prove a lifesaver for Bangkok commuters running low on battery and patience.
items.content:
A new collaboration between technology accessories brand Ugreen and the hit mobile game Honkai Star Rail is turning an everyday necessity into something far more eye catching. Leading the limited edition collection is a magnetic power bank inspired by the popular character Yao Guang, combining distinctive design with practical charging performance that could prove a lifesaver for Bangkok commuters running low on battery and patience.

Founded in Shenzhen in 2012, Ugreen has grown into a global consumer technology brand serving more than 300 million users across more than 180 countries and regions. The company has built its reputation on reliable and affordable charging products, cables, storage solutions and audio accessories that quietly keep modern life moving.

The launch comes as consumers increasingly find themselves purchasing charging accessories separately. The once familiar experience of unboxing a new smartphone complete with charger and earphones has largely disappeared. Manufacturers say the change helps reduce environmental impact, although buyers may suspect finance departments are not exactly losing sleep over the arrangement.

The result is a more demanding market, with consumers expecting faster charging, easier portability and greater convenience. Bulky chargers and tangled cables have become harder to tolerate for people juggling work, travel and social commitments throughout the day.

That is where the Honkai Star Rail collection aims to stand out. Fans of the game will instantly recognise Yao Guang, a seer strategist and general of the Xianzhou Yuque. As the game's first five star support character, she manipulates fate and grants teammates powerful extra turns. Ironically, for someone gifted with visions of the future, she still seems rather fond of a little battlefield chaos.

While gaming-themed gadgets often risk becoming little more than colourful collectibles, Ugreen's latest range offers genuine day to day usefulness.

The star attraction is undoubtedly the magnetic power bank. For commuters navigating Bangkok's BTS and MRT networks, portable charging has become almost as essential as a travel card. After all, finding a free power socket during rush hour is as unlikely as finding an empty seat.

MagFlow Air magnetic power bank Honkai: Star Rail edition

The 10,000mAh magnetic Qi2 power bank stands out for its versatile design. It combines 15W wireless charging with a built-in braided USB-C cable that doubles as a carrying strap, plus a separate USB-C port. It removes the familiar scramble through bags and backpacks when a phone battery suddenly drops into the red zone. With everything integrated into a single device, users can charge quickly without hunting for a forgotten cable. It has strong magnetic attachment, premium build quality, passthrough charging support, and the ability to charge up to 30W when using the USB-C cable instead of wireless charging.

For users spending long days away from desks and power outlets, that extra speed could make all the difference.

The power bank is a compelling alternative to competing power banks, especially because it offers both magnetic and wired charging in one compact device. While wireless charging is not the fastest available and the unit becomes warm during Qi2 charging.

The rest of the collection delivers plenty of practical appeal as well. A compact 65 watt wall charger offers fast charging for multiple devices, making it ideal for busy mornings. By the time breakfast and coffee are ready, a phone can already be significantly recharged.

Nexode retractable USB-C cable Honkai: Star Rail edition

Also included is a retractable charging cable capable of delivering up to 100 watts of power. While cables rarely generate excitement, this one earns points for avoiding the mysterious knots that somehow appear in bags and drawers despite no apparent human involvement.

items.title: Honkai: Nexus Anima is a fun creature collector with an incomprehensible story
items.summary: Honkai: Nexus Anima spins off with creature collecting auto-battling gameplay, making for a fun change of pace, though it doesn't quite fit the story.
items.content:
It’s a big deal whenever HoYoverse launches a new game. While it’s true that a new gacha game pops up almost every day, those same gacha games are almost all lifting references or mechanics wholesale from HoYoverse titles. Genshin Impact put the company on the map and shaped what modern gacha games are, and they’ve followed up that hit with Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero, each one making waves and shaking up the industry just a little bit more. It’s safe to assume that HoYoverse wants that same kind of impact from their next major title, and Honkai: Nexus Anima is certainly shaping up to be a swing in a wild new direction. Unfortunately, it’s a big swing that doesn’t fully connect at this time.

Honkai: Nexus Anima is a pretty unique mix of genres and gameplay hooks. While it’s built around creature collecting and will naturally draw comparisons to Pokémon, you aren’t then taking these monsters into turn-based 1v1 battles. Instead, you use them to dive into Teamfight Tactics-style auto battles between big teams of Anima – the creature name in this world.

I’ve always been curious about these sort of idle-battler games, but never met one that hooked me. Using that formula within the context of an anime gacha game, plus mixing in tons of cute collectable creatures, totally does it for me. At first, the depth of combat doesn’t feel particularly vast. There certainly isn’t a high skill ceiling to this style of battle, even as you start mixing in numerous abilities from your Eidos companions. It’s still satisfying to play, but there is a lack of mechanical difficulty at this stage which would need to ramp up to make for a truly satisfying and absorbing endgame.

Outside of battles, Honkai: Nexus Anima will be pretty familiar to you if you’ve dabbled in HoYoverse games. The tutorial section has you exploring some small interactive maps as your chosen protagonist, feeling pretty similar to the small zones of Zenless Zone Zero or Honkai: Star Rail. When you get into the meat of the game, though, you’re tossed into a pretty rich and wide map that combines the scale of a Genshin Impact region with modern buildings and whimsical fantasy meadows.

The game is beautiful, the map is beautiful, the characters you meet are beautiful…but I don’t quite know how to describe them. There isn’t a very clear genre or style to attach Honkai: Nexus Anima to – the other games in the Honkai line were always melting pots of influence that lean heavily toward sci-fi, and Genshin Impact feels similar with a further lean towards Japanese high-fantasy. Honkai: Nexus Anime is bright and bubbly, but impossible to place in the same way.

The story, meanwhile, is not bright or bubbly, but it’s certainly equally incomprehensible. HoYoverse games have an habit of repeating the same two-hit combo in their stories of giving you an amnesiac protagonist, and tossing you into a multidimensional, intergalactic story full of multiple tiers of entities and shadowy realms and world-ending threats and confusing proper nouns. Honkai: Nexus Anima lays it on as thick as usual, with all the gravitas of a grim sci-fi epic. This is a cutesy creature collector, though. The music is whimsical, and the menus are bubbly, but there’s a disconnect between the vibe the game seems to be cultivating and the vibe the story itself is doing. The dense multi-dimensional gacha stories are an acquired taste to start with, but it’s especially egregious here, and I didn’t feel an investment in or understanding of the world I’m exploring because of it.

And that’s a shame, because it really is so much fun to explore this world. Each Anima you bond with can be summoned outside of battles to wander around with you and bust out their unique abilities. One type can smash through walls, while another can become a hilarious improvised trampoline for you to bounce off. I was pretty addicted to the gameplay loop I found myself in, where I’d spend time exploring the world to find new Anima, then I’d dive into battles to see which ones fit together best in a team. And then, once I found a team I liked, I could set out to keep training and uncapping my favourite Anima to make them as strong as possible.

It’s so much fun to play Honkai: Nexus Anima and it’s take on the creature collecting genre, but from the closed beta test, that gets lost in the bland world and incomprehensible story. Being invested in the characters and the story is my biggest reason for picking up a gacha game, and without that, I already have one foot out the door with Honkai: Nexus Anima. I’m hopeful that, as we head towards the full release, HoYoverse can massage these problems and reel me back in.

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail 4.3 guide: Events, free Jades, & banner schedule
Giving a game another chance
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it. That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I...
items.content:
Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it.

That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I had to stop playing because of bugs. I also stopped because it was really laggy, but I realized when I started playing again this past December that I had actually originally played on the European server rather than the American one, which was why it was lagging.

Now that I’ve started playing it again for the last four months, I’m wishing I’d never quit.

The game’s story is amazing. With games like HSR where the main character is a self-insert, I tend to fully lean into that role. As such, whenever a major twist happens to a character that the main character has bonded with, I really feel it due to the immersion.

Another thing I like about the story is that HSR keeps you on your toes because it isn’t afraid to kill off playable characters.

I’d played a different game from HoYoverse before HSR, and it wouldn’t dream of killing a playable character, so I went into HSR thinking it’d be the same. That idea went out the window on my second day of playing with the first of many playable character deaths.

Because of that, you end up wanting to make sure you own your favorite characters in case you never see them in the game again. However, since HSR is a gacha game, you’re not guaranteed to get the characters you want when they’re available without spending money.

At least that’s what you’d think, but from my experience, HSR is the easiest gacha game I’ve played when it comes to getting the characters you want without spending money.

I’ve managed to get three characters I’ve wanted along with two of their exclusive items without spending money. That’s because HSR makes it really easy to get the in-game currency for pulling characters. That means if you just want to get a character for the sake of having them, you can.

In fact, I’d say HSR is probably the only gacha game where you don’t have to spend real money. I only spent money on cosmetics, but most cosmetics are free rewards from permanent events.

The only negative thing I have to say about the game is that the newer main quests are fairly long.

The latest finished questline takes 62 hours to complete, and the entire main quest line is currently over 100 hours. Because of that, if you have a busy daily schedule, it could take a while to complete. It is possible to finish in a week, but based on personal experience, I wouldn’t recommend it.

The length aside, I would highly recommend this game, especially since it’s free on PC and you don’t even need a gaming one as I play on my laptop. With the three years of content in the game so far, I can’t wait to see where it goes from here.
